newsitem.title: USA: Phelps Dodge sees robust copper demand.
newsitem.headline: Phelps Dodge sees robust copper demand.

text.p: Phelps Dodge Corp finds demand for copper is robust despite a moderate year-to-year decrease in prices, chief executive Douglas C. Yearley said Thursday.
"Inventories are low and the market continues to surprise many with much stronger prices than generally forecast," he continued.

He said the company's first quarter earnings of $2.12 per share, compared with $2.26 a year earlier, "demonstrates our continued ability to generate significant earnings and cash flow at current copper prices."

"Cash flow provided by operating activities, the principal measure of our operating performance, was $223.4 million in the first quarter of 1997, compared with $221.9 million in the 1996 first quarter, a particularly satisfying performance considering 6 percent lower copper prices than in the 1996 period," Yearley said.
The company reported sales of $1.02 billion for the latest quarter compared with $1.00 billion in the prior-year period.
It said this increase principally resulted from greater sales volumes of copper and from higher sales volumes in the wire and cable business.
